```json
          "hash": "e072d054c5b6d546cc61ddf436865ab510621a273b1957b63d3081762c518dfe"
        },
        {
          "uuid": "7ad83c78-9bab-484d-a679-9f1352ab4291",
          "created": "2023-12-22T10:20:23.845530Z",
          "name": "viewer_bom",
          "short_name": "viewer_bom",
          "meta": {
            "version": 2
          },
          "cloud_folder": "16dbfae0-3694-40c8-a86a-d5e438884cae/assembly_designs/52f251f2-dad6-4fdc-837c-f278d29cb1b7/heavy_meta/2",
          "presigned_url": "https://storage.googleapis.com/produuzit/16dbfae0-3694-40c8-a86a-d5e438884cae/assembly_designs/52f251f2-dad6-4fdc-837c-f278d29cb1b7/heavy_meta/2/viewer_bom?X-Goog-Algorithm=GOOG4-RSA-SHA256&X-Goog-Expires=3600&X-Goog-Signature=...",
          "hash": "e072d054c5b6d546cc61ddf436865ab510621a273b1957b63d3081762c518dfe"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

::: info
You can also filter by package name by adding it to the query parameters, like this: https://back.produuz.it/api/v2/cloudstorage/packages/?assembly_design=52f251f2-dad6-4fdc-837c-f278d29cb1b7&name=resources
:::

::: info
You can also get the design packages from the `client_order_id` of a constructible, with the query key `assembly_design__actuals__client_order_id` (`module_design__actuals__client_order_id` for modules).
:::

::: info
This page uses the `assembly_designs` endpoint, but the same applies to the `module_designs` endpoint.
:::

pages.title: Generate Constructibles
pages.body:
# API TUTORIAL – CREATE CONSTRUCTIBLES

### Intro

This document provides a step-by-step guide on how to create an assembly using the produuz.it API V2. The assembly creation involves several steps, including project and batch creation, finding an assembly design, and making a call to the assemblies endpoint with the required UUIDs. The workflow for modules is similar.

::: info
The base URL for the produuz.it API V2 is: **https://back.produuz.it/api/v2/**
:::

## Step 1: Project Creation/Retrieval

### ALL RETRIEVAL

If you don't have the project uuid, find it from your own data. You can fetch all the projects and look for it:

**Endpoint: /api/v2/company/projects/**

- Method: GET.
- **Request Body:** Empty.
- **Response:** Paginated list of project objects, in `results`.

**Example Response Payload**

```json
{
  "count": 3,
  "next": null,
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "ifc_parsing_setup": "b3f44b0e-2e75-45ad-8a5d-148f70883fe1",
      "btl_parsing_setup": null,
      "uuid": "0549be70-e2f5-4227-86a1-bfdb229e5460",
      "created": "2023-10-19T09:04:07.222371Z",
      "modified": "2023-10-19T09:04:07.222393Z",
      "name": "TEST_HOUSE",
      "client_name": "connectinq",
      "project_number": "test_1",
      "super_project": "Test_Street",
      "phases": ["Phase_1"],
      "meta": {},
      "delivery_date": null,
      "start_date": null,
      "archived": false
    },
    {
      //... other project
    },
    {
      //... other project
    }
  ]
}
```

### FILTERED RETRIEVAL

You can also filter them with query parameters:

**Endpoint: /api/v2/company/projects/?name=my_project**

This also returns a list, even if only one project matches the query.

### CREATION

If the project does not exist, you should create it. To create a project:

**Endpoint: /api/v2/company/projects/**

- **Method:** POST.
- **Request Body:** JSON object with project details.

- **Response:** Project details including the project UUID.

**Example Request Payload**

```json
{
  "name": "TEST_HOUSE",
  "super_project": "Test_Street",
  "client_name": "connectinq",
  "project_number": "test_1",
  "delivery_date": null,
  "start_date": null,
  "standard_library": false
}
```

**Example Response Payload**

```json
{
  "ifc_parsing_setup": "b3f44b0e-2e75-45ad-8a5d-148f70883fe1",
  "btl_parsing_setup": null,
  "uuid": "0549be70-e2f5-4227-86a1-bfdb229e5460",
  "created": "2023-10-19T09:04:07.222371Z",
  "modified": "2023-10-19T09:04:07.222393Z",
  "name": "TEST_HOUSE",
  "client_name": "connectinq",
  "project_number": "test_1",
  "super_project": "Test_Street",
  "phases": ["Phase_1"],
  "meta": {},
  "delivery_date": null,
  "start_date": null,
  "archived": false
}
```

(may contain more data in some cases)

In the "uuid" param of the response you have your new project UUID.

Note that you get a list of available "phases" in the project.

If you are looking for standard libraries (only for later assembly_design retrieval), use the endpoint **/api/v2/company/standard_libraries/** instead. The workflow is the same.

## Step 2: Batch Creation/Retrieval

Some facts about produuz.it batches:

- An assembly/module always needs a batch. If the company wants to work without batches, placeholder batches are created.
- The phase is a string. The default Phase_1 can be used for simplicity.
- The production line is set to the batch, not to the assembly/module itself. So at least one batch per desired production line will be needed in a project. (Ex: BATCH_PL1, BATCH_PL2, BATCH_PL3,…).

The company is free to organize phases and batches as it likes.

### RETRIEVAL

To retrieve batches, use the following endpoint:

**Endpoint:** /api/v2/constructibles/batches/?project=\<project_uuid\>

- **Method:** GET.
- **Request Body:** Empty.

- **Response:** Paginated list of batches including uuids.

### CREATION

To create a batch object, use the following endpoint:

**Endpoint:** /api/v2/constructibles/batches/

- **Method:** POST.
- **Request Body:** JSON object with batch details including the project UUID.

- **Response:** Batch details including the batch UUID.

**Example Request Payload**

```json
{
  "project": "0549be70-e2f5-4227-86a1-bfdb229e5460",
  "phase": "Phase_1",
  "name": "Batch_1"
}
```

**Example Response Payload**

```json
{
  "project": "0549be70-e2f5-4227-86a1-bfdb229e5460",
  "production_line": null,
  "uuid": "94d9c646-8e2d-4ac0-b073-aff1aed2b3d7",
  "created": "2023-10-19T09:24:12.082495Z",
  "modified": "2023-10-19T09:24:12.082514Z",
  "name": "Batch_1",
  "phase": "Phase_1",
  "priority": 0,
  "show_in_viewer": true,
  "start_date": null,
  "delivery_date": null,
  "pl_ordering": 0,
  "company_calculated_time": 0,
  "use_ct_schedule": false,
  "task_subset": ""
}
```

### UPDATING

Any of the fields of the batch object can be passed in the POST create request. They can also be updated later with a PUT request that holds only the fields to change (PUT is always a partial update). For example, to set a new production line on the batch:

**Endpoint:** /api/v2/constructibles/batches/94d9c646-8e2d-4ac0-b073-aff1aed2b3d7/

- **Method:** PUT.
- **Request Body:** partial JSON object.

- **Response:** Full batch.

**Example Request Payload**

```json
{
    "production_line": "b6e25a9c-bf2f-4838-ac1d-a204932a698e"
}
```

You can also pass the production line in the creation POST request.

## Step 3: Assembly Design Retrieval

Find an assembly design to reference, either from the current project or from another project. A standard library is also a project, so for standard panels pass the standard library uuid as the project uuid.

**Endpoint:** /api/v2/constructibles/assembly_designs/?project=\<project_uuid_or_stdlib_uuid\>

**Method:** GET to retrieve assembly designs.

- **Query Parameters:** Project UUID if filtering by project.
- **Response:** Paginated list of assembly designs with UUIDs.

If needed, you can also add the **name** query filter to get a shorter list:

**Endpoint:** /api/v2/constructibles/assembly_designs/?project=\<project_uuid\>&name=\<design_name\>

## Step 4: Assembly Creation

You are ready to create an assembly once you have:

- **design** : Assembly design UUID.
- **batch** : Batch UUID.

Also you may want to add:

- **client_order_id** : Order ID coming from external management system.
- **scheduled_prod_date** : Scheduled date for the production.
- **priority** : Integer that represents the priority of the assembly in the batch, or in the day for companies that manage production by date.

Make a call to the assemblies endpoint with the data:

**Endpoint:** /api/v2/constructibles/assemblies/

- **Method:** POST.
- **Request Body:** JSON object with at least basic data.
- **Response:** The full assembly JSON object.

**Example Request Payload**

```json
{
  "batch": "94d9c646-8e2d-4ac0-b073-aff1aed2b3d7",
  "design": "b715f3b3-7007-47d2-872b-20eb46d383a7",
  "scheduled_prod_date": "2023-10-19",
  "client_order_id": "or863-12"
}
```

**Example Response Payload**

```json
{
  "batch": "94d9c646-8e2d-4ac0-b073-aff1aed2b3d7",
  "module": null,
  "design": "b715f3b3-7007-47d2-872b-20eb46d383a7",
  "uuid": "8f43556f-ee33-4aaf-b0b8-028f3d3d46dd",
  "created": "2023-06-03T22:58:49.281997Z",
  "modified": "2023-06-05T08:02:21.160681Z",
  "status": "waiting",
  "stations_status": {},
  "meta": {},
  "priority": 48,
  "scheduled_prod_date": "2023-10-19",
  "client_order_id": "or863-12",
  "parent_assembly": null
}
```

## Bulk Create

Several constructibles can be created in a single request:

**Endpoint:** /api/v2/constructibles/actuals/bulk_create/

- **Method:** POST.
- **Request Body:** One creation payload, or a list of them.
- **Response:** One result per payload (a list when you sent a list).

The payload format is chosen with the `schema` query parameter, which is required. An unknown or missing schema answers `404` with `{"status": "unknown_schema"}`.

### Custom schema 1 (hm_sap)

This schema creates the constructible and gets or creates its related objects (project, standard library, design, batch). The production line must already exist. It expects the following props:

- **project** : Project number. Will pick this project, or create if does not exist.
- **projectname** : Will be used only if project creation is needed.
- **super_project** _(optional)_: Used only if project creation is needed. Defaults to `FROM_API`.
- **stdlib_number**: Standard library number. Will pick this stdlib to fetch the design. Don't pass this param, or pass it as `null` if the design is project specific.
- **article** : Assembly/Module design name. Will be used to get the design from the project. Will be created if needed for later file uploads through the web interface.
- **ordernr** : Used to fill the client_order_id in our system (a client order ID that comes from an external management system).
- **meta** : Used to fill the client_meta in our system. This meta is shown in the design detail and can be used for customizations.
- **scheduled_prod_date** : The expected production date. Used together with `production_line_client_id`; a time part, if any, is dropped.
- **production_line_client_id** _(optional)_: The Client ID of the production line in produuz.it. When provided, the system matches the order to the production line that has this Client ID configured. If no matching line is found, the request is rejected with an error. When this field is used, `operations` is not needed for line matching.
- **operations** _(legacy)_: This is a list of objects. Used to match a production line by workcenter name. If `production_line_client_id` is provided, this field is ignored for line matching. Each operation contains:
  - **workcenter** : Name of the production line in produuz.it.
  - **date** : Used as the "scheduled_prod_date" of the constructible, the expected production date from the client. Only the operation whose workcenter matches the line is read.

The constructible goes into a batch named after the production line, created in the project if it does not exist yet. A `client_order_id` (`ordernr`) that already exists is rejected.

::: tip Recommended approach
Use `production_line_client_id` instead of `operations` for line matching. Set the Client ID on each production line in the produuz.it settings, and pass it in the payload. This avoids having to match by exact production line name.
:::

**Endpoint:** /api/v2/constructibles/actuals/bulk_create/?schema=hm_sap

**Example Request Payload (using production_line_client_id)**

```json
[
  {
    "ordernr": "123",
    "article": "MW-D11-R",
    "project": "23-555",
    "projectname": "Example_Name",
    "stdlib_number": "std123456",
    "production_line_client_id": "50000012",
    "scheduled_prod_date": "2023-10-08T14:32:17.232Z",
    "meta": {
      "project": "23-555",
      "wbs": ""
    }
  }
]
```

**Example Request Payload (legacy, using operations)**

```json
[
  {
    "ordernr": "123",
    "article": "MW-D11-R",
    "project": "23-555",
    "projectname": "Example_Name",
    "stdlib_number": "std123456",
    "meta": {
      "project": "23-555",
      "wbs": ""
    },
    "operations": [
      {
        "workcenter": "WAND",
        "date": "2023-10-08T14:32:17.232Z"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

**Example Response Payload**

```json
[
  {
    "client_order_id": "3321",
    "result": "created",
    "uuid": "the-uuid-v4",
    "level": "assembly",
    "created_project": false,
    "created_stdlib": false,
    "created_design": false,
    "created_batch": true
  },
  {
    "client_order_id": "3322",
    "result": "failed",
    "detail": "Something went wrong here"
  }
  // { ...third object }
]
```

The response is `200` when every payload was created, and `400` as soon as one failed. The payloads that succeeded are still created, so read `result` on each entry before retrying.

pages.title: Reports and machine files
pages.body:
# API TUTORIAL – REPORTS

### Intro

The `bulk_launch` endpoint takes a list of report payloads and creates one report per payload. Each report belongs to a project: pass its `project` uuid, or a `project_name` (and `super_project`) to use an existing project with that name or create it.

The flow to obtain the report will be:

1. Post the report payloads and receive the UUIDs of the created report objects.
2. Check the status of each report every few seconds until it is `ready`.
3. Once `ready`, use the presigned URL to download the file from Google Cloud Storage.

### Post reports

The payload objects hold almost the same information the web interface sends when it creates a report. Each report type adds some information of its own to the `meta` field.

Parts reports (like BoMs, machine files for parts, ...) can be selected either by a list of assembly uuids in `selected_assemblies`, or by part batches: set `meta.select_by_part_batches` to `true` and list the part batch uuids in `meta.part_batches`.

Panel reports (like MOB2 files) have to be selected by the list of `selected_assemblies`.

**Endpoint: https://back.produuz.it/api/v2/reports/bulk_launch/**

- Method: POST.
- **Request Body:** List of payloads.
- **Response:** `201` with the list of created report objects in `reports`.

**Example Request Payload**

```json
[
  {
    "name": "my-test",
    "document_type": "panel_mob2",
    "project": "461f7d25-dea3-46b1-b908-5dd187e09ea0", // Direct project picking
    "project_name": "my_project_name", // If no uuid, you can provide a name for an existent or new project.
    "super_project": "my_project_folder", // If no uuid, you can provide a super_project name.
    "selected_assemblies": [
      "uuid-of-an-assembly"
      // ...
    ],
    "meta": {
      "production_line_uuid": "uuid-of-the-production-line", // Always needed for mob files
      "action_uuid": "uuid-of-the-mob-file-action", // Only needed for auto_mob2
      "fill_mob2_defaults": true, // For auto mob defaults filling
      "part_batches": []
    }
  },
  {
    //... another report payload
  },
  {
    //... another report payload
  }
]
```

**Example Response Payload**

```json
{
  "status": "successfully_enqueued",
  "reports": [
    {
      "uuid": "aa29c0b0-eb1a-4861-b5cc-e6c86a3bd665",
      "created": "2025-08-19T12:34:13.783598Z",
      "modified": "2025-08-19T12:34:13.783609Z",
      "name": "my-test",
      "username": "dev_fede",
      "document_status": "waiting",
      "document_type": "panel_mob2",
      "project": "461f7d25-dea3-46b1-b908-5dd187e09ea0",
      "meta": {
        "part_batches": [],
        "dynamic_forms": {
          /// This is automatically filled in this case for mob2 files.
        },
        "fill_mob2_defaults": true,
        "production_line_uuid": "uuid-of-the-production-line"
      },
      "selected_assemblies": [
        "uuid-of-an-assembly"
        // ...
      ],
      "selected_assembly_designs": [],
      "selected_modules": [],
      "selected_module_designs": [],
      "files": [
        {
          "uuid": "4599a741-79d9-4b23-b53d-2c6e1ca82507",
          "created": "2025-08-19T12:34:14.703943Z",
          "name": "waiting",
          "short_name": "waiting",
          "meta": {
            "status": "waiting",
            "version": 0
          },
          "cloud_folder": "461f7d25-dea3-46b1-b908-5dd187e09ea0/reports/aa29c0b0-eb1a-4861-b5cc-e6c86a3bd665/versions/0",
          "presigned_url": "https://example.file",
          "hash": ""
        }
      ],
      "last_file": {
        "uuid": "4599a741-79d9-4b23-b53d-2c6e1ca82507",
        "created": "2025-08-19T12:34:14.703943Z",
        "name": "waiting",
        "short_name": "waiting",
        "meta": {
          "status": "waiting",
          "version": 0
        },
        "cloud_folder": "461f7d25-dea3-46b1-b908-5dd187e09ea0/reports/aa29c0b0-eb1a-4861-b5cc-e6c86a3bd665/versions/0",
        "presigned_url": "https://example.file",
        "hash": ""
      }
    },
    {}, // Another report object
    {} // Another report object
  ]
}
```

### Report types ("document_type" field)

You can select from a list of document types (BoMs, machine files, ...). Some of them need a production line (`meta.production_line_uuid`), others a machine (`meta.machine_uuid`). `GET https://back.produuz.it/api/v2/reports/document_types/` returns the current list with its labels.

| document_type        | Description                  | Needs PL | Needs machine |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------- | ------------- |
| plates_bom           | Plates BoM                   | No       | No            |
| wood_bom             | Wood BoM                     | No       | No            |
| designs_bom          | Per-Design BoM               | No       | No            |
| accesories_bom       | Accesories BoM               | No       | No            |
| custom_bom           | Custom BoM                   | No       | No            |
| qr_stickers          | QR Stickers                  | No       | No            |
| rack_load_stickers   | Rack Load Stickers           | No       | No            |
| production_excel     | Production Excel             | No       | No            |
| quality_control      | Quality Control Report       | No       | No            |
| worktime_excel       | Worktime Excel               | No       | No            |
| issues               | Issues Report                | No       | No            |
| custom_woodcsv       | Custom Woods CSV             | No       | No            |
| custom_platecsv      | Custom Plates CSV            | No       | No            |
| custom_accesorycsv   | Custom Accesories CSV        | No       | No            |
| wood_btl             | BTL File [Woods]             | No       | Yes           |
| wood_btlx            | BTLx File [Woods]            | No       | Yes           |
| wood_bvx             | BVX File [Hundegger][Woods]  | No       | Yes           |
| generic_wood_csv     | Generic Wood CSV             | No       | Yes           |
| plates_xcs           | XCS Maestro File [Plates]    | No       | Yes           |
| plates_ardis         | Ardis File [Plates]          | No       | Yes           |
| plates_dxf           | DXF File [Plates]            | No       | Yes           |
| plates_ptx           | PTX File [Plates]            | No       | Yes           |
| plates_cix           | CIX Biesse File [Plates]     | No       | Yes           |
| frame_mtf            | MTF File [Roofs]             | No       | Yes           |
| frame_nailer_csv     | Frame Nails CSV              | No       | Yes           |
| sts_steel_frame_file | STS Steel Frame File         | No       | Yes           |
| frame_btl            | BTL File [Frame]             | No       | No            |
| steel_nc             | DSTV .nc File                | No       | No            |
| steel_wiscon         | WISCON Welding               | No       | No            |
| panel_mob1           | MOB v1 Machine File          | Yes      | No            |
| panel_mob2           | MOB v2 Machine File          | Yes      | No            |
| auto_mob2            | AUTO MOB v2 Machine File     | Yes      | No            |
| panel_btlx           | BTLx Frame File [Panel]      | Yes      | No            |


For `panel_mob2`, set the flag `fill_mob2_defaults` in the `meta` field to load the defaults from your machine setups. Otherwise you need to copy the `dynamic_forms` field from a real report object.

### Fetch report objects

Once a report is created, a job is enqueued to make the actual files.

Fetch each report object every few seconds until `last_file.meta.status` is `ready`. While the file is being made it reads `waiting`, then `working_42` (42 % done); `failed` means the generation failed. Once it is `ready`, download the file directly from Google Cloud Storage through the `presigned_url` of `last_file`.

**Endpoint: https://back.produuz.it/api/v2/reports/reports/uuid-of-the-report/**

- Method: GET.

::: info
Presigned URLs expire. They are refreshed automatically, so when one has expired, fetch the report object again.
:::

pages.title: IFC to MOB2 file
pages.body:
# API TUTORIAL – IFC TO MOB2 FILE

### Intro

This tutorial covers the flow most integrations ask for: **send an IFC, generate
a MOB v2 machine file, download it**.

::: info
The base URL for the produuz.it API V2 is: **https://back.produuz.it/api/v2/**
:::

There are two ways to do it, and they answer different needs:

- **[Mobfile Generator](#route-a-mobfile-generator-recommended)** — IFC in, ZIP
  out. No project, no design, no panel. This is the one to use when you only
  want the machine file.
- **[Full project flow](#route-b-full-project-flow)** — the IFC becomes a design
  and a panel inside a project, and the MOB file is a report on it. Use this
  when the panel has to be tracked, produced and reported on in produuz.it.

Everything below needs an **API Account** (Company settings → **API Accounts**)
with the **Company Manager** or **Company Admin** role. API accounts have no
password and no OTP: a company admin generates a refresh token for them with
the key button on the account row, with an expiry of up to 370 days. That is
what makes an unattended integration possible. See
[API accounts](/guide/api/#api-accounts).

Exchange the refresh token for an access token, which lasts one hour:

**Endpoint: `POST my_user/token/refresh/`**

```json
{
  "refresh": "your-refresh-token"
}
```

The response holds `access`. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access>` on every
call below, and repeat this call when it expires.

---

## Route A: Mobfile Generator (recommended)

Four calls. The tool takes the geometry file straight to the generator, using a
production line and an IFC parsing setup you name — nothing is stored as a
project, a design or a panel.

::: info License
The Mobfile Generator is a licensed module. Its screen is hidden when your
company does not have it, so check with your administrator before building on
it. See: [Mobfile Generator](/guide/management/tools/)
:::

| Step | Call | Waits for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `POST tools/jobs/` | — |
| 2 | `POST cloudstorage/packages/<input_package_uuid>/presign_for_new_file/` + `PUT` to GCS | — |
| 3 | `POST tools/jobs/<job>/submit/` | — |
| 4 | `GET tools/jobs/<job>/` | `status == "ready"` |
| 5 | `GET output_file.presigned_url` | — |

### Step 1: Create the job

**Endpoint: `POST tools/jobs/`**

```json
{
  "job_type": "mob",
  "meta": {
    "production_line": "b6e25a9c-bf2f-4838-ac1d-a204932a698e",
    "ifcps": "b3f44b0e-2e75-45ad-8a5d-148f70883fe1",
    "dynamic_forms": {
      "7c1f0f21-2b44-4f4e-9c2a-0d2a3c9e77aa": {
        "starting_side": "inside",
        "shift_mode": "command"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- `job_type` — always `"mob"`. The tool switches to `mob2` on its own when the
  line's machines are v2, and the file extension follows.
- `meta.production_line` — **required**. Its stations' machines are what the
  file is written for.
- `meta.ifcps` — the IFC parsing setup uuid, from
  `GET company/ifc_ps/`. Required for `.ifc` and `.btlx` inputs.
- `meta.dynamic_forms` — the job settings, **keyed by machine uuid**. Send `{}`
  to fall back to the schema defaults, or fill it as the interface does (below).

The response carries the job `uuid` and, most importantly,
`input_package_uuid` — that is where the IFC goes.

::: details How to fill `dynamic_forms` the way the interface does
1. `GET factories/production_lines/` → pick the line. It carries `stations`,
   a list of station uuids in order.
2. `GET factories/stations/` → for each of those stations, `machine_setup` is
   a machine uuid. Stations without one are skipped.
3. `GET factories/machines/` → for each of those machines, take
   `default_jobs.panel_mob2`.
4. Build `{"<machine uuid>": <that object>, ...}`.

These are the same settings you see under *Station Job Options* in the
Mobfile Generator form.
:::

### Step 2: Upload the file

**Endpoint: `POST cloudstorage/packages/<input_package_uuid>/presign_for_new_file/`**

```json
{
  "name": "D-10001.ifc",
  "short_name": "D-10001",
  "type": "application/octet-stream"
}
```

The response gives a `url`, a `method` and the `headers` to use:

```json
{
  "url": "https://storage.googleapis.com/...&X-Goog-Signature=a1b2c3...",
  "method": "PUT",
  "headers": { "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream" },
  "file": { "uuid": "...", "name": "D-10001.ifc" }
}
```

Send the raw file bytes with a **PUT** to that `url`, with those `headers`. The
URL expires, so request it right before uploading.

::: info
Accepted inputs: `.ifc`, `.btlx`, `.btl`, `.jjs`, `.wup`. Anything else in the
package is skipped. **Repeat this step for every file you want in the same
run** — one job takes many files and returns one ZIP holding all of them.
No `meta.section` is needed here, unlike the design upload in route B.
:::

### Step 3: Submit

**Endpoint: `POST tools/jobs/<job-uuid>/submit/`**

No body. This is what starts the generation.

It answers `400` if no input file was uploaded, and `409` if the job is already
running. A finished job can be submitted again after a `PATCH tools/jobs/<uuid>/`
on its `meta` — that is how you re-run the same file with different settings.

### Step 4: Wait

**Endpoint: `GET tools/jobs/<job-uuid>/`**

Read `status`:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `draft` | created, not submitted |
| `waiting` | queued |
| `working_42` | generating, 42 % done |
| `ready` | the ZIP is there |
| `error` | generation failed |

Poll every few seconds.

### Step 5: Download

The same response carries `output_file`, with a `presigned_url`. Download
directly from it — no authentication header needed.

```json
{
  "uuid": "...",
  "status": "ready",
  "output_file": {
    "name": "output.zip",
    "presigned_url": "https://storage.googleapis.com/..."
  }
}
```

The ZIP holds one `.mob2` (or `.mob`) per input file, the isolation CSV when the
machine produces one, and a `pics/` folder with the plots of each panel.

Presigned URLs expire. They are refreshed automatically, so if one has gone
stale just fetch the job again and use the new URL.

::: warning
A file that fails to generate is skipped, and the job still finishes `ready`
with the rest inside the ZIP. Check that the ZIP holds one file per input rather
than trusting the status alone.
:::

---

## Route B: Full project flow

Use this when the panel has to exist in produuz.it — planned, produced, reported
on. The MOB file is then a **report** on a real panel.

Two things explain the shape of it:

- A **design** is the drawing (the IFC). A **constructible** (assembly) is one
  physical panel to be produced from that design. The MOB report is launched on
  **constructibles**, so you always create both.
- The **production line** is set on the **batch**, not on the assembly.

| Step | Call | Waits for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `POST company/projects/` | — |
| 2 | `POST constructibles/assembly_designs/` | — |
| 3 | `POST cloudstorage/packages/get_or_create/` | — |
| 4 | `POST cloudstorage/packages/<pck>/presign_for_new_file/` + `PUT` to GCS | — |
| 5 | `GET constructibles/assembly_designs/<design>/` | `meta.analysis == "done"` |
| 6 | `POST constructibles/batches/` + `POST constructibles/assemblies/` | — |
| 7 | `POST reports/bulk_launch/` | — |
| 8 | `GET reports/reports/<report>/` | `last_file.meta.status == "ready"` |
| 9 | `GET last_file.presigned_url` | — |

### Steps 1 to 4: project, design, IFC

These are covered call by call in
[Upload and create designs](/tutorials/api/post_designs/). The one thing to get
right is the file meta on the presign call:

```json
{
  "name": "D-10001.ifc",
  "short_name": "D-10001",
  "type": "application/octet-stream",
  "meta": {
    "section": "assembly_ifc",
    "tipo": "timber_panel",
    "ext": "ifc",
    "status": ["uploaded"],
    "design_name": "D-10001"
  }
}
```

::: warning
`meta.section` must be exactly `assembly_ifc` (`module_ifc` for module designs).
That is the key the analysis reads. A file uploaded without it is stored, but
never parsed.
:::

### Step 5: Wait for the analysis

Uploading the IFC enqueues the analysis on its own.

**Endpoint: `GET constructibles/assembly_designs/<design-uuid>/`**

Read `meta.analysis`:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `waiting` | queued, not started |
| `working` | parsing |
| `done` | ready to produce from |
| `error_bad_setup` | parsed, but the panel orientation could not be read — check the IFC parsing setup |
| `error`, `error_no_wrapper` | the analysis failed |

::: info
Some companies have automatic analysis switched off. If `meta.analysis` stays at
`waiting`, trigger it explicitly with
`POST constructibles/designs/launch_analysis/` and the body
`{"uuids": ["<design-uuid>"]}`.
:::

### Step 6: Create the constructible

A constructible always belongs to a batch, and the batch is what carries the
production line. One batch per production line per project is the usual setup.

**Endpoint: `POST constructibles/batches/`**

```json
{
  "project": "0549be70-e2f5-4227-86a1-bfdb229e5460",
  "phase": "Phase_1",
  "name": "BATCH_PL1",
  "production_line": "b6e25a9c-bf2f-4838-ac1d-a204932a698e"
}
```

**Endpoint: `POST constructibles/assemblies/`**

```json
{
  "batch": "94d9c646-8e2d-4ac0-b073-aff1aed2b3d7",
  "design": "340c1149-7f85-4a83-bede-10089e462069",
  "scheduled_prod_date": "2025-10-19",
  "client_order_id": "or863-12"
}
```

Keep the assembly `uuid`. That is what the MOB report is launched on. See
[Generate constructibles](/tutorials/api/constructibles/) for the bulk variant.

### Step 7: Launch the MOB2 file

**Endpoint: `POST reports/bulk_launch/`**

The body is a **list** of report payloads, so several files can be launched in
one call.

```json
[
  {
    "name": "MOB2 - TEST_HOUSE - PL1",
    "document_type": "panel_mob2",
    "project": "0549be70-e2f5-4227-86a1-bfdb229e5460",
    "selected_assemblies": [
      "8f43556f-ee33-4aaf-b0b8-028f3d3d46dd"
    ],
    "meta": {
      "production_line_uuid": "b6e25a9c-bf2f-4838-ac1d-a204932a698e",
      "fill_mob2_defaults": true
    }
  }
]
```

- `selected_assemblies` — assembly (constructible) uuids, never design uuids.
- `meta.production_line_uuid` — always required for MOB files.
- `meta.fill_mob2_defaults` — fills the job settings from the machine setups of
  that line, so you do not have to send the `dynamic_forms` block yourself.

One report covers one production line. To write a file per line, send one
payload per line in the same list.

### Steps 8 and 9: wait and download

**Endpoint: `GET reports/reports/<report-uuid>/`**

Read `last_file.meta.status`: `waiting` → `working_42` → `ready` or `failed`.
Once `ready`, download from `last_file.presigned_url`.

Full detail in [Reports and machine files](/tutorials/api/reports/), including
the complete list of `document_type` values and the `auto_mob2` variant.

---

## Which route

| | Mobfile Generator | Full project flow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Calls | 4 | 9 |
| Needs a project / design / panel | No | Yes |
| Several files in one run | Yes, one ZIP | Yes, one report |
| Panel tracked in produuz.it | No | Yes |
| Output | ZIP with `.mob2` + plots | the machine file |
| Module needed | Mobfile Generator | — |

## Related

- [Upload and create designs](/tutorials/api/post_designs/)
- [Fetch and filter designs](/tutorials/api/designs/)
- [Generate constructibles](/tutorials/api/constructibles/)
- [Reports and machine files](/tutorials/api/reports/)
- [Mobfile Generator](/guide/management/tools/) — the same tool in the interface

pages.title: NiceLabel Integration
pages.body:
# NiceLabel PRINT through Webhooks

A produuz.it webhook can launch the NiceLabel **PRINT** method, so a label is printed when something happens in production, for example when a panel starts. The `nicelabel_print` payload builds the print job defined in the [NiceLabel Cloud Trigger API](https://help.nicelabel.com/hc/en-001/articles/7361208442001-Appendix-B-Cloud-trigger-API#print-method-1-5). Both NiceLabel API V1 and V2 are supported.

Go to **Production Settings → Automations**, open the **Webhooks** card and press **New**. Fill in the form:

- **Name**: a name to recognise the webhook, like `NiceLabel panel labels`.
- **events**: the events that print a label, like `constructible_start`. You can pick several.
- **Fire on every production line**: turn it on to print on every line, including lines created later. Otherwise, pick the lines in **Production lines**. With no line and the switch off, the webhook never fires.
- **Payload content**: select `nicelabel_print`. It can be combined with other blocks, but NiceLabel only needs this one.
- **auth header type**: select `None`.
- **URL**: your NiceLabel Cloud Trigger URL, like `https://labelcloudapi.onnicelabel.com/Trigger/v1/CloudTrigger/Api-CloudIntegrationDemo-Print`.
- **custom headers**: press **ADD** and add `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key` with your NiceLabel subscription key (this header may not be needed in your setup).

Once `nicelabel_print` is selected, a **Payload Extra Fields** section appears under **Payload content**. Expand it and fill in:

- **printer name**: the NiceLabel printer name, like `ZEBRA R-402`.
- **file path**: the NiceLabel label path, like `/panels/panel_label.nlbl`.
- **api version**: the NiceLabel cloud API version, `v1` or `v2`. `v2` is the default.

Your form should look like this:

![The webhook form filled in for NiceLabel](./webhook_form.svg)

1. The events that print a label.
2. The production lines it prints on. Or turn on **Fire on every production line** above it.
3. `nicelabel_print` as the payload content.
4. The **Payload Extra Fields** section that appears with it: printer, label file and API version.
5. Your NiceLabel Cloud Trigger URL.
6. The subscription key header, if your NiceLabel setup asks for one.

Press **Save**. For API V2, NiceLabel cloud receives a payload like this:

```json
{
  "event": "constructible_start",
  "deviceType": "CloudPrinter",
  "deviceId": {
    "printerName": "ZEBRA R-402"
  },
  "filePath": "/panels/panel_label.nlbl",
  "quantity": "1",
  "dataSources": [
    {
      "uuid": "e8f7e7f7-3b27-41e0-bb78-99eae64ba7cd",
      "design_uuid": "db0cb2a6-8fbf-46ac-81f5-ece6faca584e",
      "design_name": "ML-0B-5",
      "status": "waiting",
      "scheduled_prod_date": "2023-11-11",
      "client_order_id": "1030622",
      "batch_uuid": "e8986e12-4454-4ae5-a40d-4929d6a5b789",
      "batch_name": "Batch",
      "phase": "Phase_1",
      "client_meta__your_key_1": "XXXX",
      "client_meta__your_key_2": 2
    }
  ]
}
```

Each key of the panel's `client_meta` is added to the data source with the `client_meta__` prefix, so your label can use it as a variable.

For API V1, it receives this:

```json
{
  "event": "constructible_start",
  "FilePath": "/panels/panel_label.nlbl",
  "FileVersion": "",
  "Quantity": "1",
  "Printer": "ZEBRA R-402",
  "PrinterSettings": "",
  "PrintJobName": "",
  "Variables": [
    { "Name": "uuid", "Value": "e8f7e7f7-3b27-41e0-bb78-99eae64ba7cd" },
    { "Name": "design_uuid", "Value": "db0cb2a6-8fbf-46ac-81f5-ece6faca584e" },
    { "Name": "design_name", "Value": "ML-0B-5" },
    { "Name": "status", "Value": "waiting" },
    { "Name": "scheduled_prod_date", "Value": "2023-11-11" },
    { "Name": "client_order_id", "Value": "" },
    { "Name": "batch_uuid", "Value": "e8986e12-4454-4ae5-a40d-4929d6a5b789" },
    { "Name": "batch_name", "Value": "Batch 1" },
    { "Name": "phase", "Value": "Phase_1" }
  ]
}
```

The label data comes from the panel or module the event is about, so use the panel and station events (`constructible_start`, `constructible_ready`, `station_start`, `station_ready`). Every webhook body also carries the `event` key.

# CHANGELOG

[//]: # "Important!! After pushing to prod and updating this, run the following command in production."
[//]: # 'python manage.py message "Produuz.it updated" --desktop --link "https://docs.produuz.it/changelog/"'

## SOON

- 📚 **Documentation** — the old screenshots are gone. Every page now shows the screen as it is today, drawn with numbered marks that the text under it explains one by one: the production viewer and its checklist, the logistics viewer and part batches, the Delivery screen and the rack editor, production lines, machine settings, automations, the dashboard, quantities, planning, the report form and what each report looks like on paper, webhooks, the Claude connector and more. Click a picture to see it full size. The pages were also checked against the app and corrected where they had fallen behind: menu names, button labels, settings and defaults. See: [Production Viewer](/guide/viewer/)

## 2026.09.25

- 🤖 **Claude connector** — Claude can now **create an IFC parsing setup** for you. Give it the property list of a few elements from your BIM application, describe what marks a rail, a stud and a plate, and it writes the setup straight into **Company settings → IFC Parsing Setups**. It is the first and only thing the connector can create, and it is fenced in: it asks for a separate permission the first time and you can refuse it, it needs a company administrator account, it can never change a setup that already exists or make one the default, and what it creates is assigned to no project — so nothing is re-analysed and no panel moves until you open it, check it and assign it yourself. **Your production data stays read only**: no panel, part, batch, checklist or proof can be changed through the connector by any means. If you would rather nothing was written at all, deny the permission and ask for the file instead. See: [Creating a parsing setup](/guide/mcp/#creating-a-parsing-setup)
- 📐 **IFC Parsing Setup** — a setup has always been downloadable as a file and uploadable back, and there is now a page that says exactly what is inside that file: every field, every category and property key, what a rule has to look like, and a complete working example. That is how you copy a setup between companies, keep a version outside the platform, or have one written for you and bring it in finished. Uploading saves nothing on its own — the file opens in the normal editor and exists when you press **Save**. The setup guide has also been brought in step with the editor: *Hidden Material* and *Ignored Part* are class behaviours now, not categories, and *Not Isolated Area* is gone because nothing ever read it. See: [The setup file (JSON)](/guide/management/ifcps/json/)
- 📷 **QR reader** — the QR button in the left menu now opens the reader as a window over the screen you are on, instead of taking you to a page of its own. Close it and you are back where you were; with a rack open, scanning a panel marks it without leaving the rack. It uses the same camera as the checklist pictures, with a button to switch cameras on devices that have more than one. Scanning a QR for a checklist task and for an RFID tag uses the same reader.
- 📄 **BoM reports** — wood parts that differ only in their length now share **one table and one drawing** in the Wood BoM and the Per-Design BoM. The twelve studs of a sloped wall, all with the same angled top cut, used to give twelve tables whose drawings differed only in the length number; now they give one drawing, where the length reads **LENGTH**, and a row per stud with its real length. Details are measured from the end they belong to, and a part turned over or end for end counts as the same part. It is on by default and can be turned off in the report form with **Group parts that differ only in length**. In the Per-Design BoM with extended tables, custom branches set as *wood alike* now get the timber tables with drawings too, instead of a plain list. The drawing of each part in the viewer and in logistics does not change. See: [Wood BoM](/guide/reports/wood_bom/)
- 📏 **Part drawings** — the dimension numbers no longer print on top of each other. On a long part, features a few centimetres apart used to share the same spot on paper, and so did the heights of a part drawn only a few millimetres tall. On a real project that happened on more than half of the drawings. Now numbers that would touch are moved apart, and each tick bends towards its number, so every number can be read and still points to the right place. Nothing was taken off the axes. On top of that:
  - Each rectangular cutout also gets its **depth** and its **width** dimensioned right on it.
  - A set of evenly spaced drillings shows its **pitch** (*2× D22 @30*).
  - Hole labels no longer overlap each other.
  - A square end no longer prints a *0* at each corner.

  **Before**

  ![Part drawing before: numbers printed over each other](./part-drawing-labels-before.svg)

  **After**

  ![Part drawing after: numbers spread apart, cutout depth and width, drilling pitch](./part-drawing-labels-after.svg)

  Drawings are redrawn the next time the panel is analysed.
- 🐞 **Fixed** — **Part drawings:** round shapes were drawn and dimensioned as if they were polygons, with a number at every small step of their outline. Now a drilling gets its centre and diameter, and a blind one also its depth in the side view. A slot gets both round ends, each with its centre and diameter. A round notch on an edge gets its radius, its centre (even when it falls on or outside the edge), where it starts and ends, and how deep it goes. A tube or round bar gets only its diameters. The facets of round surfaces are no longer drawn as lines. Stray angles such as *178°* or *167°* read off the outline of a hole are gone. A shallow cut, such as a pocket whose floor meets the face at a small angle, now shows the line that closes it. Drawings are redrawn the next time the panel is analysed.

## 2026.09.22

- 📱 **App on your phone or tablet** — produuz.it can now be installed like an app. In Chrome on Android, open the browser menu and choose **Install app**; on an iPhone or iPad, use **Share → Add to Home Screen**. It gets its own icon on the home screen and opens **fullscreen**, with no address bar and no browser buttons, so the whole screen is the panel you are working on. It is the same produuz.it and the same login — nothing to set up, and nothing changes if you keep using it in the browser.
- 🐞 **Fixed** — **Viewer:** at companies that work by date, a production account saw the date selector twice in the left menu — once beside the account button and again above the panel list, both moving together. Only the one above the list is left, which is the one that decides what the list holds. The same duplicate was in the logistics menu. On a tablet left open for a day or more, opening a **detail, a document, a spec or a project drawing** could show an empty page: the link to the file had expired and nothing asked for a new one. Those screens now get a fresh link on their own.

## 2026.09.21

- 🔤 **Properties in texts** — the text fields that take `{property}` names now tell you which names they take. Every one of them gets an **Insert property** button that lists what you can use and drops it in at the cursor: the **viewer header**, the **viewer list hint** and the **custom constructibles column** in *Company → Viewer settings*, and the **part data fields** and **user attributes** of the BTL, BTLx and BVX machine setups. The list is not only the built-in names — it also shows **your own model properties**, read from your recent panels, which is the half nobody could guess. The machine file fields also accept the names the panel fields use, so `{super_project}`, `{batch_name}` and `{phase_name}` now work in both places. A field will no longer let you save a text whose braces do not close. And in the **Automations** trigger form, the *design field* box now offers your own model properties instead of asking you to remember them. See: [Properties in Texts](/guide/properties/)
- 📸 **Checklist pictures** — a new company setting, **Avoid native camera in viewer** (*Company → Viewer settings*). Some companies manage their tablets with a policy that blocks the camera app, and when that happens the camera button opens the photo gallery instead, with nothing to explain why. Turn this on and the app takes the picture itself, without asking the device. It applies to checklist tasks and to notes alike. Leave it off unless you have that problem: the device's own camera is the better one where it works. See: [Production Viewer](/guide/viewer/)
- 🔌 **Webhooks** — a new payload block, **serialized_project**, adds the project the event belongs to: your own **project number**, the client name, the super project and the start and delivery dates. Until now a payload named the project only by its produuz.it id, so matching an event to a job in your own system meant a second lookup. It arrives as `project__details`, and it is left out when the event has no project. See: [Integrations & Webhooks](/guide/integrations/)
- 🐞 **Fixed** — **Machine files:** a user attribute written as `{super_project}` put the words *not found* into every part of the BVX file instead of the super project name; unknown properties now come out empty, the same as in the BTL and BTLx files. **Company settings:** a mistyped text — an unclosed brace, or the `{}` the old help text suggested as an example — was accepted and then broke the viewer header, the viewer list and the constructibles table until somebody corrected it. **Machine settings:** twelve fields of the BTL and BVX setup forms were all labelled *Split files by Profile Size*, *Use voids* was filed under *User Attribute 5*, and *Bench position* opened empty instead of on its default. **Viewer:** the panel list was asking the server for the custom hint on every row even at the companies that do not use it. **Webhooks:** the delivery log painted successful calls red. Only a plain `200` counted as accepted, so an endpoint that answers `201` because it created a record, `202` because it queued the work or `204` because it has nothing to say filled the log with errors for calls that had arrived perfectly. Any `2xx` is a success now, both in the log and in the **Last delivery** column.

## 2026.09.20

- 📐 **IFC Parsing Setup** — a panel whose setup does not mark its top and bottom rails, or whose file carries no zones, could not be placed at all: its drawings came out in the coordinates of the IFC file, which for a roof element modelled on its slope means a flat projection at the wrong size, with every part in zone 0. produuz.it now works the panel out from its own geometry: the plane from the timbers, the length from which way is up, and the front face from what is on each side — battens go over the sheathing on the outside, a panel closed on one face has that face inside, and a sheet drilled with round holes for sockets and pipes is an inside layer. It draws as a panel again. Turn it on in company settings with **Best effort panel orientation** — it is off until you do, and it changes nothing for panels your setup already places. It is a best guess and the front face can come out on the wrong side, so marking the rails and the zones in the setup is what makes it certain. Machine files are untouched: they still refuse a panel they cannot place, because a guessed face would mean a mirrored panel on the machine. See: [IFC Parsing Setup](/guide/management/ifcps/)
- 🐞 **Fixed** — **Part drawings:** a long timber with a deep section — a rafter or a joist, anything from about 36 x 270 upwards — was drawn standing up instead of lying down, so it came out as a hairline down one side of the sheet with the rest of the page empty. Those parts are now drawn lying down, like every other one. The title on each drawing also showed a 32-character code instead of the short part reference used everywhere else, and the same long code reached the part tables of the cutting reports. Drawings are redrawn the next time the panel is analysed.

## 2026.09.17

- 🐞 **Fixed** — **Login:** on a computer or tablet set to dark mode, the login page drew its fields dark over the photo background, which left the boxes barely readable and the text hard to see. There is no theme switch before signing in, so the login page now always uses the light theme; your own choice of light or dark is untouched everywhere else. **Checklist and notes:** on a computer or a Windows tablet, the camera button opened the file browser instead of the camera, exactly like the button beside it. It now opens the camera on those devices too — and attaching a picture to a note uses the same two buttons as a checklist task, so the camera behaves the same way wherever you attach a photo.

## 2026.09.16

- 🔗 **API** — a new tutorial walks the whole flow end to end: send an IFC, generate its **MOB v2** file and download it, with the exact payload for every call and what to wait for between them. It covers both ways of doing it — straight through the **Mobfile Generator**, which takes the IFC and hands back the machine file with no project involved, and the full project flow, where the IFC becomes a panel you can produce and report on. It is the question integrators ask most often, and the answer was spread over three separate pages until now. See: [IFC to MOB2 file](/tutorials/api/ifc_to_mob2/)
- ⚙️ **Production settings** — the *Part classes* tab of the IFC parsing setup is now **Custom part classes**, and a class can do more than carry a name. Press **Behaviours** on it and say what parts of that class are left out of the panel measurements: the surface, the width, the height or the thickness, each on its own. The case it was built for is a **placeholder layer** — something modelled inside the panel that is not produced but takes up the space a real layer will. Ignore it in the surface, the width and the height, leave the thickness alone, and the panel keeps its real thickness while its surface stops counting a layer nobody built. Everything is off by default, so nothing changes until you turn something on, and each class row shows what it ignores without your having to open it. The **Properties** tab is now **Part properties**, which is what it always held. And in **Hierarchy and project**, the *Names* and *Project* sections are now one, **Unit and project properties** — they held the same kind of setting, and the old split put the phase and the batch outside a section called *Names* while the module id sat inside it. Nothing moved: the same six properties, in the same order, in one place. The IFC parsing tutorial has been rewritten around the seven tabs, in the order you actually set them up in. See: [Custom part classes](/guide/management/ifcps/#custom-part-classes) and [Setting Up IFC Parsing](/tutorials/ifcps/)
- 📐 **IFC Parsing Setup** — the separate *BTL Parsing Setup* is **gone**, along with its entry in the project settings: BTLx files have been read with the IFC parsing setup for a long time and the BTL one was no longer used by anything. And two things that used to be part categories are now **custom part class behaviours**: *Ignored Part* is now a class with *Ignore this part completely*, and *Hidden Material* a class with *Hide in the 3D viewer*. Your rules were moved across for you, so nothing changes in what you see. The company checkbox *Hide hidden materials in 3D* goes with them: each setup now decides for itself. A part can also belong to **several classes at once** and takes the behaviours of all of them. See: [Custom part classes](/guide/management/ifcps/#custom-part-classes)
- 🌳 **Custom part branches** — a branch now has a second switch, **Counts in the panel measurements**. A branch is recognised before a part falls back to timber or plate from its category, so a part your setup knows perfectly well — a window frame, a cladding profile — could end up with no category, and a part with no category was outside the panel width, height, thickness and surface, with nothing saying so. Turn the switch on for cladding and frames that are really part of the panel; leave it off for brackets and connectors that stick out past the frame. It is **off by default**, so nothing changes until you tick it. Which measurements the part is then left out of is still a custom part class job. Worth knowing either way: these measurements are not only a report figure — your **rack loads** are drawn from them, so the width decides how many panels fit in a rack row and the thickness how deep the stack builds. See: [Custom part branches](/guide/management/ifcps/#custom-part-branches)
- 🐞 **Fixed** — **Panel measurements:** nail lines, saw cuts, drills, milling and glue were measured as if they were part of the panel, so a saw mark hanging below the bottom rail made the panel read taller than it is, and marked areas reaching past an edge made it wider. They describe what a machine does, not what the panel is made of, and they no longer count towards any panel dimension or area. Each design picks the corrected numbers up on its next analysis. **Notes:** raising a note on a **module** never worked. The form took it, the save came back with a technical error and the app errored on top of it; nothing was ever created. Module notes are now saved on the module, they show up on it, and the link in the message sent with them opens the module instead of a page that does not exist.

## 2026.09.15

- 🧩 **Parts list** — a **Name** column, and you can search and sort by it. The name is now yours to decide: in the parsing setup, *Part Name* says which IFC property holds it, and left empty it keeps reading the name the IFC element carries, exactly as before. What the IFC file itself called the part is still kept and still visible, as its own optional column and in the part panel. See: [IFC Parsing Setup](/guide/management/ifcps/)
- ⚙️ **Production settings** — the **Part Name** property in the IFC parsing setup, so the name shown in the parts list, the reports and the machine file templates can come from the property your exporter actually writes. It does not change how parts are classified: the category and branch rules keep matching the raw IFC properties. The documentation now also spells out how the **Zone** property reads a layer written with a letter — `F1`, `F2` on one face and `B1`, `B2` on the other — where the `B` is what makes the zone negative. The **assembly filter** is back, and it now has two lists: *Split only these assemblies* keeps what you name and leaves the rest of the file alone, and *Never split these assemblies* drops what you name even when the first list keeps it. Both lists apply to the new hierarchy splitter as well, which ignored the filter until now. Leave them empty and every assembly is split, as before. And every rule and every property name gains a **Read from a specific property set** box, for when the same property name exists in two property sets with different values: name the set to read, or tick it and leave it empty to read only the IFC element's own attributes. The editor's tabs are reordered to follow the order you set things up in, starting with **Hierarchy and project**, and two of them are renamed to say what they hold: **Panel Part Categories** and **Steel Cage Part Categories**. The whole guide has been rewritten around the editor, with every setting documented and reachable from its own (i) button. See: [IFC Parsing Setup](/guide/management/ifcps/)
- 🔌 **Webhooks** — a webhook can now react to **several events at once**, so one endpoint no longer needs a row per event repeating the same URL, secret and headers. Your existing webhooks keep exactly the event they had. A new event, **station start**, fires when an operator starts a station, not only when the station is finished. Calls are now made in the background, so a slow endpoint of yours can no longer hold up the tablets on the shop floor — expect the call a few seconds after the event, and do not rely on the order of two events raised together. You see it on the panel, in the **Production Proof** card of the constructible detail page, and in the **Quality Control Report**, under each picture. Pictures uploaded before this say *No author recorded* rather than borrowing a name. See: [Quality Control Report](/guide/reports/quality_control/)

- Fixed: TOP/FRONT arrows on wood side views pointing at the wrong faces, slow response when many users connect at once, client info overlapping the divider on Dymo QR labels, wrong module numbers when loading splitter counts into the matrix, and wrong drawing counts in the designs table.
